links.outcome: Acceptability (AIM score) and distress after using the AYA-RISE chatbot
links.effect: Acceptability threshold exceeded, with post-test AIM score >4 by 80% of AYAs; no significant change in distress thermometer scores (pre 3.4, post 3.6, p=.34).
links.quote: Our threshold for acceptability was exceeded, with a post-test Acceptability of Intervention Measure (AIM) score of > 4 by 80% of AYAs.

links.outcome: Feasibility and acceptability of a chatbot developed with AYAs, family members, and clinicians
links.effect: Co-developed with 17 AYAs plus families and clinicians; in pilot, 100% used the intervention through risk information presentation and 80% had AIM >4.
links.quote: The intervention was developed together with AYAs with cancer risk syndromes, their family members, and clinicians, using Invitae’s Gia® chatbot (study Phase 1).

unlisted_practices: Co-designed chatbot for cancer genetic risk communication to improve patient knowledge

screen.reason: Evaluates the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary outcomes of a patient-facing chatbot (Gia-based AYA-RISE intervention) used by adolescents and young adults in cancer risk communication.
